title: 80% of the Deal Is Over Before the Buyer Talks to Sales
summary: Braydan Young co-founded Sendoso and grew it past a thousand employees, then left to fix the one part of selling he could never make move fast enough: getting a prospect on the phone with a real customer. His argument is that roughly 80% of a B2B deal is finished before the buyer ever requests a demo, so the reference call belongs at the front of the process instead of bolted on at the end. He walks through how SlashExperts works, why a paid and disclosed reference beats a static G2 review, why the references who admit implementation was painful close deals faster, and the numbers he is seeing so far: 60-day cycles landing in 15 to 20 days, plus roughly a 10% lift in deal size. Worth listening to if you run a sales team that still spends the last two weeks of the quarter scrambling for a customer who will pick up the phone.
keyQuote: You've already looked at the reviews. You've already probably talked to a user, and you've done so many of those things, which we call 80% of the deal cycle, before you actually go and talk to sales.
guestBio: Braydan Young graduated into the 2009 job market and started out selling insurance in San Francisco, where his boss told him a hundred-year-old company does not do webinars. He moved into tech sales, worked as an SDR and an AE at companies including Demandforce and Mya Systems, and in 2014 launched a side project called Coffee Sender that let reps drop Starbucks gift cards into cold emails. Coffee Sender became Sendoso, where he spent close to a decade as co-founder and head of growth and watched headcount go from roughly 60 people to a thousand during COVID. He now runs SlashExperts, which raised a $2M seed round in April 2025 and connects prospects directly with a vendor's existing customers for peer reference calls. He also invests through Launch 639 Ventures.
takeaways: 80% of the deal is done before the buyer ever talks to sales.
G2 reviews are static. Buyers trust a peer on the phone instead.
References belong at the top of the funnel, not the end of it.
Deals with a reference call close 2x faster: 60 days to 20.
A reference who admits implementation hurt closes deals faster.
Cap how often a reference takes calls or you will burn them out.
The discovery call is dead. Show up knowing their stack.
